RSPCA appeals for adopters as centres come under strain

5 hrs ago
RSPCA
Pets
By Frankie Crew Reporter

Share

0 comments

'We urgently need help' - RSPCA seeks homes for rescued animals

Colette (Image: RSPCA)

Skip to next photo

'We urgently need help' - RSPCA seeks homes for rescued animals

The RSPCA is appealing for “extra-special adopters” across Hampshire as it faces a surge in multi-animal rescue cases.

So far this year, 114 cases involving 10 or more animals at a single address have been recorded in the county, nearly matching the 116 total for all of last year.

Many of the animals have complex behavioural and medical needs.

Jo Rowland, chief executive for the RSPCA, said: "We are struggling and we urgently need help.

Mowgli (Image: RSPCA)

Read more

Hampshire and Isle of Wight ranked among UK Premium Bonds hotspots
Pensioners could miss out on £300 Winter Fuel Payment despite being the right age
Hampshire hand first professional contracts to teenage cricketers O’Neill and Patil

"Our frontline officers are finding dozens, even hundreds of animals in need at single addresses.

"We are getting amazing support from other animal charities and our brilliant network of RSPCA branches but we are all under immense strain.

"We need to get pets out of our centres and into loving homes so we can continue to rescue."

The RSPCA is working with Inspiring Vet Care to rehabilitate animals and support rehoming during its annual Adoptober campaign.

Jo Rowland said: "We are encouraging people to contact an animal charity if they are at a stage where they, or someone they know, is struggling with the numbers of animals they have in their household.

"The sooner actions are taken the better for animals and people."

Simba (Image: RSPCA)

The RSPCA Ashley Heath Animal Centre in Ringwood currently has several animals looking for homes, including two cats and three dogs.

Animal centre manager Claire Rowe said: "Jemima is such a gentle giant and is full of affection, playfulness and is very smart too."

Jelly is described as a “sensitive soul” who is currently with a staff foster carer.

Ms Rowe said: "We just love Jelly and although we love having her around, we can’t wait to see her head off into a home of her own."

Simba, a three-year-old French Bulldog, has recovered in RSPCA care after arriving emaciated.

Ms Rowe said: "Simba’s rough start in life hasn’t squashed his spirit.

"He shares his vibrant energy and affection with everyone he encounters, regardless of whether they are humans or dogs of any size."

The RSPCA is asking experienced and patient pet owners to consider adopting or fostering to help free up space in its centres.

Colette (Image: RSPCA)

Ms Rowland said: "We really need help from animal lovers.

"If you are considering adding a pet to your home, please consider rescuing - and if you can’t adopt, could you consider fostering?

"We need extra special homes for some of our animals and we’re so grateful to anyone who can support our Adoptober campaign."

To enquire about adopting or fostering one of the animals, visit the RSPCA website at rspca.org.uk and complete an online application form.
